title: Why · How · What
caption: A long chat blurs in the middle, for a different reason than a long phone call: what fills the window, and how to see it.

why.title: The AI forgets what you told it an hour ago.
why.caption: <marker>Think of a long phone call: you remember how it began, how it ended and one odd moment, and the middle blurs.</marker> A long chat blurs the same way.

how.title: Attention thins out as the window fills.
how.caption: <marker>Every message goes in again, and the first lines and the newest messages draw the most attention; the middle and the rest fade.</marker>

what.title: Far more than your chat sits in the window.
what.caption: <marker>Saved memory loads at the start, a web search drops whole pages in, and near the limit the app may summarise old messages.</marker> Try every part and control below.

why.description: In free recall of a word list, the first and the last items are remembered best and the middle worst, and an item that stands out is remembered better than its neighbours [1][2]. This is lab evidence from word lists, so applying it to a long call or chat is an inference (research COG-0001).

murdock-serial-position.title: Murdock, The serial position effect of free recall

glanzer-cunitz-two-stores.title: Glanzer and Cunitz, Two storage mechanisms in free recall

how.description: Models use information best at the start and end of the input and worst in the middle, and the first tokens draw strong attention even when they mean nothing [1][2]. Quality also falls as the window fills, even with perfect retrieval [3][4]. The strength differs per model, and the mechanism is the authors' account, not proof for every product (research LLM-0006, LLM-0007).

du-length-alone-hurts.title: Du et al., Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval

what.description: Claude Code loads its memory at the start of every conversation, as context that counts against the window [1]. A search tool returns page content that sits in the window as input tokens [2]. Near the limit the Claude app summarises earlier messages; for other apps no vendor documents it [3] (research LLM-0008, LLM-0009, LLM-0010).
